title: Circuit-breaker state lives only in module memory: a restart silently clears a trip and its acknowledgement trail, so the protection against a misfiring detector is lost on every restart

evidence.note: triggerHistory, trippedChains and recentTriggerEvents are in-memory Map/Set; the module has no DB read or write
header: exits stay disabled "until the operator resets the breaker through the dashboard (Plan 19-06) or CLI"
a real reset logs resetByOperatorTs and broadcasts cb_reset; a restart produces neither
the ring buffer exists so the reset modal shows exactly the events that tripped the breaker
the reset route refuses unless tripped; :88 serves the ring buffer
evaluation filters in-memory timestamps; after a restart the history is empty
contrast: the dry-run start stamp is persisted precisely so that a restart does not reset it
only api/routes/antiRug.ts calls it; the CLI reset named in the header does not exist
codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Restarting the process clears a manual-reset-only breaker

sibling_sites_checked: All module-local anti-rug state: circuitBreaker.ts:73-83 and detector.ts:192 (positionRegistry), :197 (chainState), :247 (pendingV3Burn). The registry and pending maps are rebuilt at boot by resumeAntiRugMonitoring (bot.ts:1989-2145); the breaker is not. A duplicate module load would split all of these maps (RC-17, owned by the TX slice, noted here only). _resetRegistryForTesting (detector.ts:301) and _resetForTesting (circuitBreaker.ts:228) have no production caller (git grep at the base).
severity_rationale: S2. The breaker exists to stop a misfiring detector from selling one position after another (exitTrigger.ts:32-35). After a restart the same code and config run with an empty history, so up to `threshold` more emergency sells at minOut 0 can go out before it trips again. Bounded per position; live mode only. The opposite effect (a restart re-enables anti-rug after a trip caused by AUD-ANTIRUG-003) is today the only reset besides the dashboard.

traces.scenario: Restart after the circuit breaker tripped (is the reset intended, or a lost protection?)
steps: Live mode. The threshold-th incrementCircuitBreaker on a chain (circuitBreaker.ts:110-128) adds the chain to trippedChains, logs fatal, broadcasts cb_tripped and sends [ANTI-RUG HALTED] (:130-161).
Every later trigger on that chain returns at exitTrigger.ts:221-232 with a log.fatal only.
The bot exits: an operator restart, a SIGINT, or a crash such as AUD-ANTIRUG-002 or AUD-BUY-005. Nothing in circuitBreaker.ts is written to disk.

Boot: module load creates empty maps (circuitBreaker.ts:73-83). resumeAntiRugMonitoring re-registers positions and arms the listeners (bot.ts:2074-2144). isCircuitBreakerTripped returns false for every chain (:171-173); getRecentTriggers returns [] (:215-218), so the dashboard has no halted state and the reset modal has nothing to acknowledge. Nothing at boot reports that a chain had tripped.

The next trigger on that chain sends a live exit. The breaker trips again only after `threshold` new triggers, and the threshold-th exit has already been sent by then (increment after the exit, exitTrigger.ts:312-319).
traces.outcome: Judgment: the restart reset loses a protection the design relies on; it is not an intended reset. Evidence: the header promises the trip lasts "until the operator resets" it (circuitBreaker.ts:5-7); the acknowledgement trail is built for that reset (ring buffer :30-36, reset log and broadcast :183-203, reset route and modal data antiRug.ts:59-67, :88); and the codebase persists gate state it means to survive restarts (db.ts:691-696). A restart is not an acknowledgement: it can follow a crash, and nothing tells the operator after boot that a chain had tripped.

recommendation: Persist the trip (chain_state or its own table), restore it at boot, require the dashboard reset to clear it, and alert at boot when a chain starts tripped; either build the CLI reset the header promises or remove the claim. Card ANTIRUG-04. Phase 24.
